key_insight: Explainable registry-based models predicted chronic GVHD better than acute GVHD, but external performance and calibration varied widely across cohorts.
clinical_relevance: For allo-HSCT care, these models may help risk-stratify chronic GVHD, but they are not yet reliable enough for uncalibrated clinical use, especially for acute GVHD.
method: Trained gradient boosting models on three CIBMTR registry-derived datasets (N=2,509).
Externally tested in six cohorts (N=14,788), including a Middle Eastern cohort.
Evaluated discrimination, calibration (intercept/slope, Brier score), and SHAP-based feature explanations.
evidence_signal: Internal AUROC was 0.736 for chronic GVHD and 0.624 for acute GVHD; externally, chronic remained modestly predictive (AUROC 0.54–0.64) while acute fell near chance (0.52–0.57) with frequent calibration drift.
watch_item: Training performance did not predict external calibration behavior, so cohort-specific recalibration and local validation are essential before implementation.
paper_title: External Evaluation and Calibration Drift of Explainable Machine Learning Models for Acute and Chronic GVHD Prediction After Allogeneic HSCT
